analysis.title: GS Global Equities Call 3 Nov 2026
key_insights: US futures mixed pre-market (SPX -15bps, NDX +25bps, RTY -15bps) ahead of the US Midterm Elections. Prediction markets imply a 90%+ chance Democrats win the House and a 65%+ chance they win the Senate.

Overnight, the US and Iran were reported to be reviewing mediator proposals, while the US reportedly struck targets on Iran's Qeshm Island. The NYT described it as a small-scale defense measure with no immediate plans to escalate. WTI rose 2% to $98.50 after falling 8% the prior day.
AAPL fell 4% pre-market after earnings as investors focused on higher memory costs weighing on gross margins. PLTR fell 8% after guiding to a slowdown in bookings growth.
Pre-market earnings today include APO, ETN, FISV and SHOP. AMD, ANET, BKG and SMCI report after the close.

GS says investor attention to the midterms is dampened this year because of other catalysts (AI re-rating and capital markets, geopolitics). Democrats need to gain only 3 House seats, and Republicans hold nearly 30 seats in districts Trump won by less than 11pp.
The Senate race looks closer but likely matters less for policy because 60 votes are needed for most legislation. A Democratic Senate could block presidential nominees.
GS expects historical election-versus-equity patterns to be even less useful this cycle, since recent political uncertainty has been unrelated to legislative developments.

Since 1954, the 12 months after a midterm have been the strongest stretch of the four-year cycle for the S&P 500. Across 18 midterms the index averaged +7.5% through year end, +13.9% over 6 months and +15.5% over 12 months, and was higher at both points every time. Other years averaged +4.3% (6m) and +7.2% (12m).

Median 12-month S&P 500 returns are 13% under divided government versus 9% under unified control, so a sweep may have less broad market impact than many suggest. Renewables, ACA beneficiaries and government spending ex-defense stand to benefit from a Democratic sweep.

Short leverage on the GS PB book remains near YTD highs despite last week's short de-grossing. GS calls it a tailwind through the midterms, buybacks coming out of blackout and positive November seasonality.

Breadth: 70% of S&P members rose yesterday. S&P equal weight has outperformed the cap-weighted index by 2.95% over 5 sessions, the best run YTD outside July's AI drawdown (peak spread 3.87%). About 67% of S&P members trade above their 50-day average, up from about 21% in September, against a YTD high of 72%.
October hedge fund performance: Fundamental L/S -3.5% and Systematic L/S -3.6%, the first time since 2016 on GS records that both fell 3% or more in a month.

October single-stock flows were net sold, with long sales outpacing short sales 4 to 1. Info Tech, Industrials and Materials were the most net sold sectors. Consumer Discretionary, Real Estate and Health Care were the most net bought. Index and ETF products were net bought (1.6 to 1).

Net leverage fell at the fastest pace since March while gross leverage rose on mark-to-market. Fundamental L/S net leverage fell, led by Asia L/S funds. HFs rotated out of TMT and Cyclicals into Defensives.

Buyback desk activity ran 0.6x 2025 YTD ADTV and 0.7x 2024 YTD ADTV. Mix shifted to 22% open market versus 78% 10b5-1 (prior week 16%/84%). About 60% of the S&P 500 is in an open window, rising to about 82% by the end of the week. GS expects November flows to pick up toward year-end repurchase targets.
Yesterday's floor activity was 3 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were moderate net sellers (tech-led) and HFs moderate net buyers (cover demand in industrials, tech and healthcare).

Chart of the day: real forward rates have shifted higher twice. The first came from late 2024 and was cemented by the April 2025 tariffs, taking longer-dated forwards above 2023 highs. A sustained break into new territory came in July 2026.
